jurisdiction.name: Albania
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Albania has no AI law in force. Public-sector AI use rests on the 2023 Law on e-governance, which defines AI and regulates its use by public bodies, and on a 2024 Council of Ministers decision setting an AI methodology and technical standards; the Digital Agenda 2022-2026 and the 2025-2030 education digital agenda add AI objectives. A draft AI law aligned with the EU AI Act was put to public consultation in May-June 2026 and a draft National AI Strategy 2025-2030 in 2025; neither has been adopted. Albania is a party to the Council of Europe's data protection convention (Convention 108), and Parliament approved ratification of the Council of Europe AI Convention in September 2026.
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 and 13 October 2026 from the official legal database (qbz.gov.al) and the government consultation portal; a run cut off by a usage limit was resumed and its downloads re-read against the official texts. Not yet verified from official texts: any AI guidance from the data protection commissioner and any AI bills before Parliament. The 2024 data protection law, whose publication date could not be confirmed, and the AI Convention ratification law are tracked as leads.

instruments.issuing_authority: National Agency for Information Society (AKSHI), as draft law of the Council of Ministers
instruments.current_status: Published for public consultation by AKSHI on the national e-consultation register (RENJK no. 982) for 20 working days, 29.05.2026 to 26.06.2026, with public meetings on 11 and 17 June 2026 (consultative document). No later stage (adoption by the Council of Ministers or submission to the Assembly) was found on 2026-10-13. If enacted it would enter into force 15 days after publication in the Fletorja Zyrtare (draft art. 106). Consultation closed on 26 June 2026.
instruments.summary: Draft framework AI law of 106 articles and 13 annexes that its explanatory report says follows the structure of the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689). It would set harmonised rules for placing AI systems on the market and using them, ban certain AI practices (with conditions on real-time remote biometric identification for law enforcement), set requirements for high-risk systems and transparency and general-purpose AI model obligations, create market surveillance, a national AI-system register and AI regulatory sandboxes, with fines. It names AKSHI as coordinating authority and the Information and Data Protection Commissioner among the competent authorities, and gives 12-24 month transition periods.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Albania's proposed horizontal AI law aligning with the EU AI Act.

instruments.summary: Draft first national AI strategy, 'AI Strategy 2030: Leap towards Wellbeing', setting a vision of AI 'made in Albania, for Albania' that is ethical, safe and inclusive. It reviews AI use in public administration, a SWOT analysis and high-potential sectors (public services, health, education, agriculture), and sets six pillars (infrastructure and ecosystem, AI in industry, education and workforce, regulatory framework, data as a strategic enabler, international cooperation) with a maturity roadmap and action plan. It builds on Law 43/2023 on e-governance and the 2024 AI methodology and technical standards (VKM 479/2024) and aligns with the Digital Agenda and the S3 smart specialisation strategy.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Draft national AI strategy; would be the first dedicated AI strategy once approved by the Council of Ministers.

instruments.english_title: Council of Ministers Decision No. 479 of 24 July 2024 on the approval of the methodology and technical standards for the use of artificial intelligence in the Republic of Albania
instruments.current_status: Published in Fletorja Zyrtare no. 130 of 29.07.2024 and in force immediately under point 2 of the decision, i.e. from its adoption on 24.7.2024. No amendment found.
instruments.summary: Decision adopted under art. 39(2) of Law 43/2023 approving a methodology and technical standards for using AI technology in Albania, drawing on NIST AI RMF 1.0, OECD and EU practice. The annex sets purpose and scope, standards, principles, risks and challenges, guidance and monitoring of AI implementation, including documentation and impact assessment of AI-based changes to information systems. AKSHI, ministries and other public institutions are charged with implementing it.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Albania's main in-force AI-specific rulebook for AI use in public information systems.

instruments.summary: General e-governance law that defines artificial intelligence (art. 4(16): the simulation of human intelligence processes through computer systems and algorithms). Art. 39 provides that AI technology is to be applied, where possible, in public ICT systems to support innovation in the digital economy, and requires the Council of Ministers to set a methodology and technical standards for its use, which it did with VKM 479/2024.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Statutory basis for public-sector AI use and for the AI methodology and standards.

instruments.current_status: Published in Fletorja Zyrtare no. 84 of 05.06.2022 (qbz metadata); the decision enters into force on publication. Covers 2022-2026; no successor digital agenda found.
instruments.summary: Cross-sectoral digital strategy for 2022-2026 that aims to drive investment in advanced computing, data processing, AI, cybersecurity and advanced digital skills. Its platforms pillar includes a dedicated objective (6.5.2) on AI platforms: enabling AI use in public-sector projects and services to deliver proactive services, with a high-performance computing centre and big-data/machine-learning analysis of government data. Implementation is assigned to AKSHI and the ministries named in the action plan.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current digital strategy with an AI pillar; the draft AI strategy 2025-2030 is designed to align with it.

instruments.summary: Education-sector digital action plan whose Objective 3 is to enable and encourage innovative technologies such as AI. It commits the Ministry of Education to develop and apply guidelines and practical cases for the ethical and effective use of generative AI in education (measure 8) and to include AI in the pre-university ICT curriculum (measure 10), alongside teacher digital-skills training.

coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-13, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. idp.al firewall blocks curl; parlament.al not searched directly; qbz.gov.al live search/gazette timed out 2026-10-13 (qbz texts saved 2026-10-12 used). Resumed run: existing records re-checked and corrected. VKM 479/2024 effective 2024-07-24 ('hyn në fuqi menjëherë', in force on adoption). Law 43/2023 effective 2023-07-19 computed from art. 59 (15 days after publication 2023-07-04). Placeholder orgs o-989490370aa0, o-40a8f10b72e6 pruned. Law 93/2026 (CoE AI Convention ratification, decree 512 of 6 Oct 2026) lead pending gazette publication. Convention 108: Law 9288 of 7 Oct 2004 (decree 4375 of 26 Oct 2004). Units covered: Law: qbz.gov.al (official gazette/legislation portal) searched for AI terms (198 acts reviewed on 2026-10-12); Law 43/2023 (AI article) recorded; Law 124/2024 (automated decisions) and Law 93/2026 (CoE AI Convention ratification) held as leads pending gazette dates; no AI-specific law in force; draft AI law at consultation stage; no bill found before the Assembly.; Government: AKSHI/e-consultation portal: draft AI strategy 2025-2030 and draft AI law recorded; Council of Ministers AI methodology VKM 479/2024 and Digital Agenda 2022-2026 recorded; no adopted AI strategy found.; Ministries: Education: Digital Agenda for Education action plan (GenAI guidelines foreseen) recorded; defence/security, procurement, cyber strategies mention AI only in passing (leads); health, justice, finance, labour, interior: searched via qbz, nothing AI-specific found.; Regulators: Information and Data Protection Commissioner (idp.al blocks curl; web search found no AI guidance document, only information-request replies); Bank of Albania, AMF, AKEP, AKSK (cyber): searched, nothing AI-specific found.. Not reached: idp.al site pages (WAF blocks curl; only search-engine discovery); parlament.al (not searched directly); qbz.gov.al live search on 2026-10-13 (timeouts). Could not verify: Gazette publication date of Law 124/2024 (qbz.gov.al timeouts; held as lead).; Whether the draft AI strategy or draft AI law advanced after consultation (no official record found).; idp.al AI guidance (site blocks automated access).. procurement, cyber-security, data-privacy, standards, index-readiness, international, historical: no material found.

leads.issuing_authority: Assembly of the Republic of Albania
leads.note: GDPR-aligned data protection law (adopted 19.12.2024, promulgated by decree no. 5 of 15.1.2025); art. 20 gives the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions including profiling, and arts. 13-14 require information on the logic of automated decision-making. Full official text read (idp.al copy https://idp.al/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/ligj-2024-12-19-124.pdf; qbz ELI https://qbz.gov.al/eli/ligj/2024/12/19/124). The gazette publication date could not be confirmed on an official source on 2026-10-13 (qbz.gov.al search and gazette endpoints timed out; the text itself carries no publication date; a non-official snippet says Fletorja Zyrtare 2025 no. 9). Promote as a data-privacy binding_law record once the gazette date is confirmed (in force 15 days after publication, art. 101).
